value.title: Extreme rays and diameter conjecture for the oriented-multicut skeleton
value.statement:
Let $QMET_n$ be the cone of quasi-semimetrics and $OMCUT_n$ the cone generated by oriented multicuts. Let $G_{OMCUT_n}$ be the skeleton graph of $OMCUT_n$, whose nodes are its extreme rays and whose edges join adjacent extreme rays. A **dominating clique** is a complete subgraph such that every node is adjacent to at least one of its elements.

**Oriented-multicut skeleton conjecture.** (i) All oriented multicuts are extreme rays of $QMET_n$. (ii) The oriented cuts form a dominating clique in $G_{OMCUT_n}$; consequently, the diameter of $G_{OMCUT_n}$ is $2$ or $3$ for every $n\geq 4$.

The assertions were presented as conjectural general results about the oriented-multicut cone; the surrounding text does not provide a general proof or resolution.
value.source_name: M. Deza, M. Dutour and E. Panteleeva, “Small cones of oriented semi-metrics”, arXiv:math/0111145 (2002).
value.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0111145

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2001).

value.title: Adjacency and diameter conjecture for the ridge graph of the quasi-semimetric cone
value.statement:
Let $QMET_n$ be the cone of quasi-semimetrics, with triangle facets, non-negativity facets $NN_{ij}$, and ridge graph $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ whose nodes are the facets of $QMET_n$ and whose edges join adjacent facets. Two vectors are **conflicting** if they have components with nonzero values of different signs.

**Adjacency and diameter conjecture.** (i) A triangle facet is adjacent to a facet if and only if they are non-conflicting. (ii) The non-negativity facets $NN_{ij}$ and $NN_{i'j'}$ are adjacent if and only if neither $i'=j$ nor $j'=i$. (iii) The diameter of $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ is $2$. (iv) The ridge graph $G^{*}_{QMET_n}$ is an induced subgraph of $G^{*}_{OMCUT_n}$.

These assertions were checked by computer for $n\leq 7$. The diameter assertion follows formally from the proposed adjacency criteria together with the preceding non-adjacency results, but the general adjacency and induced-subgraph claims remain open.

value.title: Facet classification conjecture for the oriented-multicut cone
value.statement:
Let $OMCUT_n$ be the cone of oriented multicuts. A **zero-extension** of an inequality on $OMCUT_{n-1}$ is the inequality obtained by adding a zero coordinate for the new element. Let $H(b)$ denote a hypermetric inequality, and let $A_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ and $B_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ be the inequalities defined in the paper.

**Oriented-multicut facet conjecture.** The following inequalities define facets of $OMCUT_n$: (i) zero-extensions of every facet of $OMCUT_{n-1}$, including oriented triangle and non-negativity inequalities; (ii) every hypermetric inequality $H(b)$ except non-oriented triangle inequalities; and (iii) the inequalities $A_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$ and $B_n(c_1,\dots,c_{n-2};a,b)$.

The conjecture was checked by computer for $n\leq 7$. Its completeness as a facet description in general remains open.

value.title: Composition-dependence conjecture for maps between resonance complexes
value.literal_statement:
For every $n\geq 1$, let $\operatorname{Res}\,\lambda$ denote the resonance set associated with a number partition $\lambda$ of length $n$. If $\operatorname{Res}\,\tilde\lambda\geq\operatorname{Res}\,\lambda$, choose compositions $\tilde\alpha$ and $\alpha$ of types $\tilde\lambda$ and $\lambda$, respectively, whose resonance sets satisfy the required inclusion. This choice induces a map

$$
\gamma(\tilde\alpha,\alpha):\delta_{\tilde\lambda}\rightarrow\delta_\lambda
$$

and hence a homology map

$$
\gamma(\tilde\alpha,\alpha)_*:\widetilde H_*(\delta_{\tilde\lambda})\rightarrow\widetilde H_*(\delta_\lambda).
$$
 **Composition-dependence conjecture.** The isomorphism type of $\gamma(\tilde\alpha,\alpha)_*$ depends not only on the actual number partitions $\tilde\lambda$ and $\lambda$, rather than their sets of resonances, but even on the choice of the pair of compositions $\alpha$ and $\tilde\alpha$. Thus the induced homology map is not determined solely by the resonance data or by the number partitions.

value.title: Vertically symmetric nest distribution conjecture
value.statement:
Let $(a)_k=\Gamma(a+k)/\Gamma(a)$, let $G=G^{\rm V}_{2n}$ be the vertically symmetric fully packed loop grid, and let $P_G(k)$ denote the number of diagrams with $k$ nests. Define

$$
A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(3j+2)\frac{(6j+3)!(2j+1)!}{(4j+2)!(4j+3)!}=1,3,26,646,\ldots.
$$

**Vertically symmetric nest distribution conjecture.** The nest distribution is

$$
P_G(k)=k\frac{4^{n+k}}{27^n}\frac{(1/2)_{n+k}}{(1/3)_{2n}}\frac{(3n+1)!(2n-k-1)!}{n!(n-k)!(2n+k+1)!}A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}.
$$

Here $A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}$ is the number of vertically symmetric $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ ASMs. The conjecture was checked for $n$ up to $8$, but remains unresolved in the supplied text.
value.source_name: Jan de Gier, “Loops, matchings and alternating-sign matrices”, arXiv:math/0211285 (2003).
value.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211285

value.title: Natural algebra action on matchings for alternating Kasteleyn matrices
value.literal: Let $A$ be a nonsingular alternating matrix, and let $D$ be the matrix-algebra deformation of $\mathbb{C}[\operatorname{coker} A]$ defined by the twisted relations in the paper. Let $G$ be a planar graph with nonempty matching set $P$, and suppose that $A$ is a Kasteleyn matrix of $G$. **Kasteleyn algebra-action conjecture.** There is a natural action of $D$ on $\mathbb{C}[P]$, possibly depending on how $G$ is embedded in the plane. Such an action would provide the algebraic structure underlying the proposed quantum-bijection interpretation of perfect matchings. The source gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

value.title: The conjecture that knot-generated graphs differ from graphs with polynomial one
value.literal:
Let ${\cal C}_1$ be the set of graphs isotopic to planar graphs, ${\cal C}_2$ the set of graphs isotopic to graphs obtained from planar graphs by the specified moves, ${\cal C}_3$ the set of graphs isotopic to graphs obtained from knots, including the unknot, by those moves, and ${\cal C}_4$ the set of graphs whose polynomial $P$ equals $1$. The known inclusions are ${\cal C}_1\subseteq{\cal C}_2\subseteq{\cal C}_3\subseteq{\cal C}_4$.

**The conjecture that ${\cal C}_3$ and ${\cal C}_4$ differ.**

$$
{\cal C}_3\neq{\cal C}_4.
$$

This asserts that not every graph with polynomial $P=1$ can be obtained from a knot by the specified moves. The paper presents the question alongside the established inclusions but gives no proof or resolution of this separation.

value.title: Freeness conjecture for the equivariant cohomology of a graph

literal_gate.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with axial function $\alpha$, let $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ be its equivariant cohomology ring, and let ${\mathbb S}({\mathfrak g}^*)$ be the polynomial ring occurring as the ring of constant maps. For a generic $\xi\in{\mathfrak g}$, let $\sigma_p$ be the number of ascending edges terminating at a vertex $p$, and let $b_k(\Gamma)$ be the number of vertices with $\sigma_p=k$. **Freeness conjecture.** $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ is a free ${\mathbb S}({\mathfrak g}^*)$-module with $b_k(\Gamma)$ generators of degree $k$. This is one of the paper's Morse-theoretic conjectures concerning the equivariant cohomology ring of a graph; the supplied text gives no resolution status or further supporting context.
